text: In a UK Biobank analysis, the authors report that machine learning models trained on accelerometry data distinguished clinically diagnosed Parkinson's disease (n = 153) with an AUPRC of 0.14 ± 0.04, and prodromal Parkinson's disease (n = 113) up to 7 years pre-diagnosis with an AUPRC of 0.07 ± 0.03, from the general population (n = 33,009), outperforming models based on genetics, lifestyle, blood biochemistry or prodromal symptoms data. (low confidence)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: The 95th centile of stride velocity has been approved by the EMA as a primary endpoint for assessing ambulant patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, a regulatory precedent in a disease other than Parkinson's disease. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-17)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: The Mobilise-D consortium's perspective paper on regulatory qualification of wearable sensors to quantify real-world mobility performance in patients affected by Parkinson’s Disease reports that its qualification strategy and both the technical and clinical validation plans received highly supportive qualification advice from the European Medicines Agency. (low confidence)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: Four reviews each point to standardization needs: a Movement Disorders systematic review of early Parkinson's disease calls for standardized study methodologies, a scoping review of prodromal Parkinson's disease says future research should prioritize standardized assessment, a real-world walking speed review says adoption requires improved standardization of devices, algorithms, and study methodologies, and a review of digital biomarkers for precision diagnosis and monitoring notes a lack of standardized data verification protocols. (high confidence)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: A scoping review of prodromal Parkinson's disease and a systematic review of wearable sensors for early diagnosis each report that most included studies were cross-sectional. (medium confidence)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: A three-round consensus study of 12 experts from the Mobilise-D consortium’s Parkinson’s Disease Working Group reached full consensus on a clinical utility framework for digital mobility outcomes with three main categories. (low confidence)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: In a systematic review of longitudinal studies in early Parkinson's disease, the authors report that three DHTs detected longitudinal changes when scales did not, with one study showing larger effect sizes for change over time of selected DHT features compared to rating scales. (low confidence)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: WATCH-PD was a 12-month, multicenter observational study in which 82 individuals with early, untreated PD and 50 age-matched controls wore research-grade sensors, a smartwatch, and a smartphone while performing standardized assessments in the clinic. (medium confidence)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: In WATCH-PD, participants wore the smartwatch at home for seven days after each clinic visit and completed motor, speech and cognitive tasks on the smartphone every other week. (low confidence)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: In WATCH-PD, the authors report that device-derived features, particularly arm swing, the proportion of time with tremor, and finger tapping, differed significantly between individuals with early PD and age-matched controls and had variable correlation with traditional assessments. (low confidence)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: The registry record for WATCH-PD, NCT03681015, lists the overall status as COMPLETED, with a status verified date of 2022-09. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-01)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: In a systematic review of real-world walking speed across conditions, the authors report that no device or outcome measure that assesses walking speed in real-world conditions has been fully validated by the FDA, and that they found four letters of intent on the FDA website related to this concept. (low confidence)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD

text: In the consensus study, the authors report that the main challenge to address is the definition of clear reference value for DMOs interpretability. (low confidence)
keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD
